slides.title: This Is Not Pay-for-Play
slides.subtitle: Trust grows when people can collaborate without being treated as sales leads.

bullets.text: Engineers come together to solve challenges in an open environment.
Useful participation matters more than promotional spend.
OCP does not sell Community contact information.
What you get out reflects what you put into the Community.

figure.alt: A trusted OCP Community space containing useful participation, open collaboration, and room to solve hard problems; sales-first behavior remains outside.
figure.caption: The trusted environment works when participation and collaboration serve the shared problem—not a sales funnel.

slides.title: Participation Builds Credibility
slides.subtitle: Open collaboration connects technical progress with durable brand trust.

cards.title: Innovate

slides.title: Listen First in Project Workstreams
slides.subtitle: Relevance and patience come before visibility.

bullets.text: Identify projects and workstreams connected to your organization's expertise.
Join regular calls with the people who can help solve the technical problem.
Listen for priorities, constraints, decision patterns, and existing relationships.
Contribute where your experience can move shared work forward.
Consider volunteer leadership after trust and momentum are established.

figure.alt: Five-step sequence: find the relevant workstream, join and listen, learn priorities and context, offer useful help, and lead after trust is established.
figure.caption: Visibility is the result of the sequence, not the first step.

slides.title: Trust Is the Brand Asset
items: Treat OCP as a trusted engineering community, not an advertising channel.
Begin in the workstreams that match your organization's expertise.
Listen before deciding how you can help.
Contribute useful work in many possible formats.
Collaborate with others and let leadership follow demonstrated value.

slides.title: Build Trust in the Right Order
slides.subtitle: Answer each question once to continue. Correctness is not required, and you can retry.

questions.prompt: Your organization is new to an OCP workstream. What is the strongest first move?

choices.text: Join the relevant calls, listen for the group's priorities, and learn how the workstream operates.
Ask for the participant contact list so the sales team can introduce itself.
choices.feedback_incorrect: OCP does not sell Community contact information, and a sales-first approach undermines the trusted environment.

choices.text: Open with a product pitch before learning what problems the group is solving.
choices.feedback_incorrect: A product pitch skips the context and trust that come from listening and useful participation.

questions.feedback_correct: Correct. Listening first reveals the group's needs, relationships, and working style before you decide how to help.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Start by listening in the relevant workstream. Learn the context before offering a solution.

questions.prompt: Which behaviors can build durable trust in the OCP Community? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Contribute a useful case study grounded in real OCP work.
Collaborate with other organizations on a shared problem.
Help a workstream make progress before seeking visibility.
Treat sponsorship as a substitute for participation and contribution.

questions.feedback_correct: Correct. Useful work, collaboration, and service to the workstream create the foundation for earned visibility.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Look for behaviors that help the Community solve problems. Spending alone does not create trust.

slides.thank_you_message: Nice work - you've finished Module 1: Earn Trust Before You Amplify.

slides.title: Channels You Will Use with Purpose
slides.subtitle: By the end of this module, you will be able to:
objectives: Choose an OCP channel that fits a specific goal and audience.
Recognize the durable OCP event families and use live event resources.
Apply OCP's newsworthiness filter to potential content.
Build a simple plan that moves from useful work to appropriate reach.

slides.title: Make Solutions Discoverable
slides.subtitle: Help qualified adopters find OCP-aligned products, facilities, and services.

bullets.text: The Marketplace brings together approved Solution Providers and OCP-aligned offerings.
Hundreds of members are Solution Providers, with around 1,000 Marketplace listings.
The referenced average click-through rate is 1.68% to provider sites and contact information.
OCP helps interested visitors reach providers rather than selling products itself.

figure.caption: OCP refers interest; Solution Providers deliver the offering.

cards.title: Third-party events
cards.body: Industry conferences where OCP may need Community speakers, workshops, or tracks.

cards.title: Speak
cards.body: Submit useful content during calls for presentations.

cards.title: Host
cards.body: Offer a facility, a date, or a creative Community experience.

cards.title: Sponsor

cards.title: Newsletter

slides.title: Teach What the Community Needs Next
slides.subtitle: Turn hard-won knowledge into durable, accessible learning.

bullets.text: Learners can explore open infrastructure topics on their own schedule.
The catalog spans technical and Community learning in multiple languages.
Editable course sources let the Community inspect, improve, and extend learning materials.
Useful education can preserve expertise and help the next participant succeed.

figure.alt: Knowledge from real OCP work becomes durable Academy learning, helps the next learner, and returns as stronger Community participation.
figure.caption: OCP Academy turns hard-won knowledge into reusable learning that strengthens future participation.

slides.title: Newsworthy, Useful, and Grounded in OCP Activity
slides.subtitle: A strong story helps the Community understand progress or solve a problem.

cards.title: Project activity
cards.body: Progress from an OCP project, subproject, or workstream.

cards.title: Contributions
cards.body: Specifications, reference architectures, white papers, or other approved work.

cards.title: Evidence
cards.body: Case studies, success stories, and milestones with a useful lesson.

cards.title: Marketplace alignment
cards.body: Products, services, or facilities connected to relevant OCP work.

cards.title: Partnership
cards.body: A collaborative result involving several Community organizations.

cards.title: Not a commercial
cards.body: Generic promotion without Community value does not fit OCP channels.

slides.title: Earned Reach Outlasts Advertising
items: Use the Marketplace to make OCP-aligned solutions discoverable.
Choose the event family and participation method that fit the story.
Match the message to the right communication or education channel.
Apply the newsworthiness filter before asking OCP to amplify content.
Let every channel extend useful work rather than repeat generic promotion.

slides.title: Pick the Right Path
slides.subtitle: Answer each question once to continue. Correctness is not required, and you can retry.

questions.prompt: Your team has a joint case study based on real OCP work. What is the strongest first communication path?

choices.text: Share it with the relevant workstream, then choose an OCP channel that fits the audience and story.
Send a generic advertisement to every available Community channel at once.
choices.feedback_incorrect: Broad promotion ignores relevance and the editorial standard. Start with the workstream and a channel matched to the story.

choices.text: Wait until an event date is printed in a course and use that date indefinitely.
choices.feedback_incorrect: Event schedules change. Use the live event pages and select the opportunity that fits the content.

questions.feedback_correct: Correct. Begin close to the work, then extend the story through the channel that best serves the intended audience.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Use relevance first: validate the story with the workstream, then select the right current channel.

questions.prompt: Which content is likely to meet the OCP editorial filter? Select all that apply.

choices.text: A milestone from an active OCP workstream with a useful lesson.
A collaborative case study involving several Community organizations.
An educational resource grounded in a real technical challenge.
A commercial message unrelated to OCP activity or Community needs.

questions.feedback_correct: Correct. OCP channels favor useful progress, evidence, education, and collaboration grounded in Community activity.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Look for content that rewards the Community's attention with relevant progress, evidence, or education.
